title: NRC dynamic roof study — air intrusion with and without a deck-level air retarder
jurisdiction: NRC Dynamic Roofing Facility, Ottawa, Ontario, Canada (research setup; no permit jurisdiction)
code_edition: Unknown; no project code edition is stated.

facts.text: The paper compares mechanically attached low-slope roof assemblies with and without an air retarder at deck level; it distinguishes wind-driven air intrusion into the roof assembly from air leakage through a building envelope.

The tested assembly uses a 0.76 mm (22-gauge) corrugated steel deck, 50 mm polyisocyanurate boards attached with eight fasteners per board, and a 45-mil reinforced PVC membrane 1,981 mm wide, fastened at 305 mm spacing along seams.
The specimens were tested at NRC’s Dynamic Roofing Facility under the CSA A123.21 dynamic wind uplift protocol.
The authors attribute air intrusion to membrane billowing and pressure changes in the space beneath the membrane; they identify a deck-level air retarder as a way to reduce it.

limitations: The source compares two NRC test assemblies and protocols; it does not evaluate any actual building or establish a code acceptance decision.
